title: Exact primitive discriminant -19 norm self-sums: complete proof and certificate scope

sources.author: James S. Milne
sources.title: Algebraic Number Theory
statements_used: Theorem 4.3, printed p.70 / PDF p.72: every ideal class has an integral representative of norm at most (2/pi)*sqrt(19) < 3. Since 2 is inert in Q(sqrt(-19)), only norm one is possible.
sources.inspection_scope: Actual retained v3.08 theorem statement inspected in this continuation. The discriminant -19 specialization, inert-prime exclusion at norm two, and primitive ideal orientations are proved in the new note.

sources.author: John Voight
sources.title: Quaternion Algebras
statements_used: Theorem 15.5.5 and Example 15.5.7, printed p.241 / PDF p.261: for p = 19, B = (-19,-1) has discriminant 19 and O = Z[(1+i)/2] + Z[(1+i)/2]j is maximal.

Theorem 25.1.1, printed p.403 / PDF p.423: projective maximal-order unit mass phi(19)/12 = 3/2. Principal projective stabilizer size 2 gives Haar class probability 1/3, not a class-number-one assertion.
Main Theorem 14.7.4, printed p.226: rational reduced norms of a definite rational quaternion algebra are all positive rationals; used to identify the global norm-character quotient.
Main Theorem 28.5.3, printed p.473: strong approximation for the norm-one group when S contains a split noncompact place; removes character-at-a-split-place constituents.

Propositions 41.3.1 and 41.3.6, printed pp.756-757: all-integral-ideal degree sigma(m), relatively prime multiplicativity and unramified prime-power recurrence. Principal scalars act trivially over Q and on projective markings.
sources.inspection_scope: Actual retained statements inspected in this continuation. Complete ideal-class quotient, inverse-unit measure, auxiliary-prime injectivity including p=3, and flag-reversal normalization checked in the new proof. Deep theorems remain imports.

sources.author: Pierre Deligne
sources.title: La conjecture de Weil. I
statements_used: Theorem 8.2, printed p.302 / PDF p.31: for a normalized primitive cuspidal modular form of weight k >= 2, arbitrary level N and character epsilon, the roots of T^2 - a_p T + epsilon(p)p^(k-1) have absolute value p^((k-1)/2) whenever p does not divide N. Applied at k=2 and trivial central character; old spaces at other primes have the same unramified roots.
Theorem 1.6, PDF p.5: purity for smooth projective varieties over finite fields, as used in the existing transfer proof.
sources.inspection_scope: Actual theorem text inspected; Theorem 8.2 page also rendered and visually checked to verify its exact formula and arbitrary-level scope. No full independent proof of the classical theorem is claimed.

spectral_dependency.statement: On the complement of all global reduced-norm characters, the all-integral-ideal operator T_m has norm <= tau(m)*sqrt(m) for indices coprime to the algebra discriminant and auxiliary/nonmaximal levels; normalized unramified roots have unit absolute value and product one.
spectral_dependency.application_hypotheses: Maximal discriminant-19 order; retain all ideal classes with principal Haar probability 1/3. Fine quotients at odd inert p and at ramified 19 have trivial stabilizers; the ramified quotient has 30 points. Exactly two global norm characters at each single auxiliary level and one at full maximal level. All Hecke indices are prime to 19 and to their own auxiliary level; target-dividing inert primes use anisotropic scaling instead.
spectral_dependency.normalization: M19.5-M19.12 give mass, marked ideal-flag reversal, four generators per principal ideal, odd-component scalar subtraction, coarse return correlation and the two local bad-point bounds.
spectral_dependency.theta_scope: No explicit theta/newform identity, no level-19 a_2 specialization, and no auxiliary-level cusp cancellation are needed. The generic filtered Delta bound is used on every space.
spectral_dependency.direct_primary_root_statement: Deligne Weil I, Theorem 8.2, is explicitly cited in M19 independently of the older Bourbaki realization route.

exact_classification.core: C+C = {n >= 2: n even, 19 does not divide n} minus {4,20}
exact_classification.primitive: P+P = {N >= 2: N even, 361 does not divide N} minus {4,76,380}
exact_classification.primitive_value_identity: P = C disjoint_union 19C; C contains 1 and all positive integers supported on split primes for Q(sqrt(-19)).
exact_classification.exceptional_quotient_families: n=4p and n=20p for a split prime p; the generic E <= (100/9)n^(-1/2) bound covers their terms at least 2^30.
exact_classification.finite_membership_completeness: M19.21: character +1 and no inert prime divisor <= sqrt(segment upper). At most one larger inert factor can remain and it would force character -1. The deterministic segmented checker reconstructs every required mask; hashes are supplementary.
exact_classification.descent: A least additional core exception is either entirely inert-supported or has a split prime quotient equal to 4 or 20. The analytic core and thin-family bounds exclude all possibilities above finite coverage. At ramified targets, 19m in P+P iff m in C+C; 20=1+19 removes the unramified core exception 20.
